task.title: Decide whether Workbench belongs in this repository
task.description:
Workbench (https://github.com/tylerkilgore/workbench) is an Electron shell around Workbook: point it at a folder, import repositories as projects, and get one window with every project's board in a sidebar plus a merged queue across all of them. It runs a real `workbook serve` per project — one board, one checkout, edited in place — and bundles the CLI so an install is self-contained.

The proposal is to move it into this repository under `desktop/` and retire `tylerkilgore/workbench`. This task is the decision. Nothing else in this series should start before it is answered, which is why they all depend on it.

## Why it wants to be here

Workbench builds the CLI from source and bundles it, so it has to name a revision. Today that pin is a **fork** of this repository, not this repository:

    "workbook": {
      "repository": "https://github.com/tylerkilgore/workbook.git",
      "ref": "f01514d..."
    }

It points there because the app needs Windows to build at all (#129) and carries a board change (#130). That is not a healthy place for it to stay: it means the desktop app ships a Workbook that is not Workbook.

#129 and #130 landing fixes the pin. Moving the app in removes the concept — in-tree, `scripts/build-workbook.sh` builds from the same checkout it was tagged from, so the shell and the CLI it ships cannot drift and there is no revision to remember to bump.

A second, smaller reason: packaging Workbench has been a good adversarial test of the board. #129, #130 and the dark mode in #131/#132 all came out of it.

## What this repository would be taking on

Stated plainly, because this is the part that matters.

- **A second toolchain** — Node 22 and `npm ci` in CI, and `electron-builder`.
- **A second release train**, and the artifacts it publishes: DMG/ZIP, AppImage/deb, NSIS.
- **Signing.** Windows installers are signed through Azure Trusted Signing when six repository secrets are present, and are unsigned when they are not, so that degrades rather than breaks. macOS builds are ad-hoc signed and **not notarized** — currently "open it once from the Finder context menu" software. Not wanting an unnotarized bundle carrying this project's name is a good reason to say no.
- **Go as a build-time dependency of the desktop build**, since it compiles the CLI. No Go in the shipped app.

The encouraging precedent is that this repository is already polyglot: `site/` is not Go, and `ci.yml` already knows how to skip the Go verification for changes that cannot affect it.

## The questions

1. **Do you want this at all?** A no costs nothing that is not already useful — #129 through #132 stand either way, and the fork pin is fixed by #129/#130 regardless.
2. **Are you willing to own the signing story**, including an unnotarized macOS bundle under this project's name? The alternative is shipping macOS unsigned and unlisted, with Windows the only signed target.
3. **One version or two?** Proposed: one, on the grounds that a desktop app bundling a specific CLI is more honestly described by that CLI's version than by a number of its own. Independent versions are less coupled; no strong feeling.
4. **`desktop/` or `apps/desktop/`?** No opinion — happy to match whatever you would pick if you were adding a second one later.
